questions.question_text: I was just diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and I have questions on options of treatment. I would greatly appreciate it if you could get back to me as soon as possible. Thank you.

rubric_items.description: The response should include overview of staging of pancreas cancer and how treatment options correspond to each stage
The response should include the concept of resectability and that for those tumors surgery is preferred

The response should specify that for metastatic or unresectable pancreas cancer chemotherapy is the backbone of treatment and that the main regimens used are FOLFIRINOX or Gemcitabine + Nab-Paclitaxel
The response should include radiation as a potential treatment option for localized disease
The response should include immunotherapy and that its role is currently limited to patients with mismatch repair deficiency or high microsatellite instability
The response should include targeted therapy such as PARPi for patients with BRCA mutations
The response should introduce the concept of clinical trials and the role for them in management of pancreas cancer
The response should include the importance of supportive care for treatment of pancreatic cancer which can include evaluation by palliative care specialist and nutritional support

questions.question_text: My friend has just been told they have a tumor extending from their pancreas that is wrapped around the celiac artery. I am trying to help them find pancreatic cancer specialists in the area.

The response must emphasize the need for evaluation by a multidisciplinary clinic, including surgical, medical, and radiation oncology, and clearly state that neoadjuvant treatment may be proposed to shrink the tumor to a resectable size, but some tumors may remain unresectable and only amenable to systemic therapy or radiation.
The response must explicitly state that some specialized centers can offer vascular reconstruction for tumors involving major blood vessels.
The response must provide a direct link to a list of NCI-designated cancer centers.
The response must offer to search for high-volume pancreatic cancer programs by preferred location, asking for specific location details to tailor recommendations.

questions.question_text: My loved one has been on chemotherapy for 6 months and the CA 19-9 levels are not going down. Does this mean the treatment isn't working?

questions.question_text: My father had the Whipple procedure and now has diabetes. Is this normal? How do we manage this?

rubric_items.description: The response should state that it is not an unexpected outcome as removing pancreas tissue will also take the islet cells which produce insulin

The response can state that the incidence of post whipple diabetes can vary based on how much of the pancreas is removed and the specific patient population but that it can occur in 15-20 to up to 50% of patients
The response should state the control of diabetes is achieved through regulating glucose intake via dietary modifications and medications that can help control blood sugars
The response should state that the father of the question writer should be evaluated by an endocrinologist and that he may ultimately require insulin injections to regulate his blood sugars

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and is losing weight very rapidly despite trying to eat. What can we do?

rubric_items.description: The response must explicitly state that anorexia and weight loss are common symptoms of pancreatic cancer. Synonyms for "anorexia" include "loss of appetite" and "reduced appetite."
The response must mention pancreatic enzyme replacement as an intervention and suggest discussing it with the healthcare team. Synonyms for "replacement" include "supplementation" and "therapy."

The response must recommend consulting a registered dietitian specializing in oncology for personalized nutritional advice. Synonyms for "consulting" include "seeking advice from" and "getting a consultation with."
The response must advise consuming nutrient-dense foods and suggest eating smaller, more frequent meals. Synonyms for "nutrient-dense" include "high-calorie" and "calorie-rich."
The response must suggest nutritional supplementation with high-calorie meal replacement shakes. Synonyms for "supplementation" include "adding" and "including."

questions.question_text: My mother was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and the doctor mentioned that she has jaundice. What does this mean and how is it treated?

rubric_items.description: The answer must specify that jaundice is due to an increase in bilirubin in the blood. Synonyms for bilirubin include "bile pigment" or "yellow pigment."
The answer must state that jaundice refers to a yellowing of the skin and eyes due to elevated bilirubin levels. Synonyms for yellowing include "discoloration" or "tint."
The answer must state that jaundice can arise in pancreatic cancer due to blockage of the bile duct from tumor growth. Synonyms for blockage include "obstruction" or "impediment."

The answer must state that ERCP (Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography) is used to visualize the blocked duct and place a stent to relieve the blockage. Synonyms for stent include "tube" or "support."
The answer must state that other options to relieve the obstruction include percutaneous biliary drainage or surgery. Synonyms for drainage include "release" or "removal."
The answer must state that another potential cause for jaundice is metastatic disease in the liver. Synonyms for metastatic include "spread" or "secondary."
The answer must state that treating the cancer with chemotherapy can shrink the tumor and help address the jaundice. Synonyms for shrink include "reduce" or "diminish."

questions.question_text: My husband has pancreatic cancer and is experiencing severe pain. What are the options for pain management?

rubric_items.description: The answer should express sympathy for the diagnosis and symptoms
The answer should state that one option for pain management is to use pain medications such as opioids
The answer should state that adjunctive non-opioid medications can be amitriptyline and gabapentin can be used
The answer should state that a celiac plexus block can be done to help control pain
The answer should state that steroids can also be used such as dexamethasone
The answer should state that radiation can also be used for local treatment and pain control
The answer should state that complementary therapies such as acupuncture and massages can also be pursued
The answer should state that the patient should be seen by a palliative care specialist

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we've been told the tumor is "unresectable." What does this mean exactly?

rubric_items.description: The answer should offer sympathy for the loved one's diagnosis
The answer should state that resectability is determined by the surgeons' assessment of his or her ability to safely remove the entire tumor
The answer should state tumors are deemed to not be resectable if they involve surrounding major blood vessels such as the SMA, SMV, CA, PV
The answer should state that invasion of nearby organs can also lead to a tumor not being able to be resected
The answer should state that sometimes tumors that are not initially able to be resected can be shrunk (downstaged) with chemotherapy and/or radiation and later removed

questions.question_text: My family member with pancreatic cancer is considering stopping treatment and focusing on quality of life. How do we make this decision?

rubric_items.description: The response should offer sympathy and state that it is a very difficult decision to try to make
The response should state that not everyone will make the same decision as it is a personal choice based on priorities and goals
The response should state that the decision should be made weighing the expected benefit of more therapy with the current side effects
The response should suggest meeting with the patient's oncologist and palliative physician to help make the decision

questions.question_text: My father has pancreatic cancer and was told he has a KRAS mutation. What does this mean for his treatment?

rubric_items.description: The response should state that KRAS mutations are frequently implicated in pancreas cancer as a major driver of tumorigenesis
The response should state that first line of treatment would remain standard of care with chemotherapy regimens such as FOLFIRINOX and gemcitabine/abraxane
The answer should state that there are several KRAS mutations (G12C, G12D, G12V) and they should specify which one is present in the patient's case
The response should state that targeted therapy to the KRAS mutation is an active area of research and that there may be clinical trials open that he could enroll in

questions.question_text: Are there studies for pancreatic cancer evaluating infusion of high vitamin C doses in conjunction with chemotherapy?

rubric_items.description: The response must explicitly state that high-dose vitamin C has not been proven to improve outcomes in pancreatic or any other cancer. Synonyms for "not proven" include "inconclusive," "not established," and "unverified."

The response must mention that high-dose vitamin C can act as a pro-oxidant, leading to the generation of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and enhanced killing of cancer cells. Synonyms for "pro-oxidant" include "oxidative" and "reactive oxygen species."

The response must state that there is limited published data showing high-dose vitamin C is well tolerated and shows a trend toward efficacy, but studies are limited and not sufficiently powered. Synonyms for "limited" include "insufficient," "restricted," and "small-scale."

questions.question_text: Yesterday it was confirmed that my loved one has pancreatic cancer. It is believed to be stage IV and has spread to the liver. However, they were not able to confirm cancer in the liver based on the biopsy. How can this be confirmed?

questions.question_text: Does eating vegan stall cancer progression?

questions.question_text: How do oncologists choose between gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel and FOLFIRINOX?

rubric_items.description: The response should state that typically patients that are more medically fit will be offered FOLFIRINOX whereas those patients that are more frail but still candidates for treatment will be offered gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel
The response should state that medical fitness is scored by the oncologist using the ECOG or Karnofsky performance status
The response should state that generally FOLFIRINOX is reserved for patients with an ECOG score of 0-1 whereas Gemcitabine nab-paclitaxel can be given to ECOG 2 patients

The response should state the reason that FOLFIRINOX is reserved for patients with good performance status is that it is more intensive and is associated with higher rates of severe side effects such as neutropenia, fatigue, and diarrhea

questions.question_text: What makes pancreatic cancer resectable?

rubric_items.description: The response should state that resectability is determined by the ability of the surgeon to safely remove the entire tumor and not leave any behind (R0 resection)
The response should state that involvement of major blood vessels such as the SMA, SMV, CA, PV are often implicated when a tumor is deemed to not be resectable
The response should state that for pancreas cancer to be resectable there must not be any distant metastases

The response should state that occasionally tumors that contact the veins (PV/SMV) and have less than 180 degrees of involvement can still be resected provided it can be safely removed and the vessel can be reconstructed as needed

The response should state that some tumors are deemed to be borderline resectable and that the patient will be recommended to undergo treatment with chemotherapy and/or radiation in order to attempt to down-stage the tumor and make it amenable to resection

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're worried about the financial burden of treatment. What resources are available?

rubric_items.description: The response should offer sympathy for the stressful situation dealing with financial burden during cancer treatment

The response should link to cancer specific organizations such as the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network, American Cancer Society, and CancerCare which can link to resources and financial assistance programs
The response should state that they should consult the social work team
